title: Limits · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: Account limits as retrieved: Free is 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU, 50 subrequests, and 5 cron triggers; Paid is unlimited requests, 5 min CPU (default 30 s; cron intervals of 1 hour or more get 15 min CPU), 10,000 subrequests, and 1,000 cron triggers. Memory is 128 MB per isolate on both plans. Waiting on fetch does not count as CPU time. Cron wall time is 15 minutes.

title: Cron Triggers · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: Cron Triggers map a five-field cron expression to a Worker's scheduled() handler and run in UTC. Supported fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and weekday, including Quartz-like L, W, and #. Examples include every minute and 59 23 LW * *. The page points to Workers limits for the account cap on triggers.

title: Scheduled Handler · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: The scheduled handler is scheduled(controller, env, ctx). controller.cron is the cron string that fired the event, and controller.scheduledTime is the scheduled instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC.

title: Workers · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: Free includes 100,000 requests per day and 10 ms CPU per invocation. Paid (Standard) includes 10 million requests per month then $0.30 per extra million, and 30 million CPU milliseconds per month then $0.02 per extra million CPU milliseconds.

title: Spending limits · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: A Workers spending limit covers requests and CPU time after included usage and, once it takes effect, rejects new HTTP requests, Cron Triggers, queue consumers, email Workers, and Worker-to-Worker calls. Visitors can see error 1103. The limit is not an exact bill cap because usage can continue while reporting catches up.

title: Run Workers for up to 5 minutes of CPU-time
takeaway: Changelog dated March 26, 2025: Workers can opt into up to 5 minutes (300,000 ms) of CPU time per request via limits.cpu_ms. The default remains 30 seconds. Time spent waiting on subrequests is not CPU time; wall-clock time while waiting was already unlimited.

title: Configuration · Cloudflare Workers docs
takeaway: Wrangler limits.cpu_ms sets the maximum CPU time per invocation, with a documented maximum of 300,000 milliseconds (5 minutes). The same limits object can set a subrequests cap. The retrieved section did not state a numeric default or explicitly say the setting is Paid-only.

title: Limits · Cloudflare Workers KV docs
takeaway: Workers KV keys are limited to 512 bytes and values to 25 MiB. Workers KV Instant uses a 300-byte key limit and a 1 MB total namespace, and list pagination is not supported.

title: Limits · Cloudflare D1 docs
takeaway: D1 database size is 500 MB on Free and 10 GB on Workers Paid. Free allows 10 databases per account; Paid allows 1,000,000, with the first 100,000 included. Maximum SQL query duration is 30 seconds and the maximum query result size is 50 MB.

title: Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions - GitHub Docs
takeaway: on.schedule uses POSIX five-field cron. Operators are *, comma, hyphen, and /. Schedules run in UTC unless an IANA timezone is set. They run on the latest commit of the default branch. The shortest interval is once every 5 minutes.

title: Events that trigger workflows - GitHub Docs
takeaway: The schedule event only runs if the workflow file is on the default branch. It can be delayed at high load, especially at the start of each hour, and queued jobs may be dropped. Public-repo schedules are disabled after 60 days with no repository activity. Default timezone is UTC, with an optional IANA timezone. Minimum interval is 5 minutes.

title: Disabling and enabling a workflow - GitHub Docs
takeaway: In a public repository, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled when no repository activity has occurred in 60 days. Re-enable from the repository Actions tab by opening the workflow and choosing Enable workflow.

title: crontab - schedule periodic background work
takeaway: POSIX crontab entries have five schedule fields then a command: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), and day of week (0-6, 0 and 7 Sunday). Patterns may be *, a number, a range, or a comma list. GitHub documents this as the cron syntax it uses; GitHub itself does not use the sixth command field.

title: False discovery rate - Wikipedia
takeaway: FDR is the expected share of rejected nulls that are false, FP/(FP+TP). The Benjamini–Hochberg step-up procedure finds the largest k whose ordered p-value lies on or below a line of slope alpha/m and rejects hypotheses 1 through k. BH is valid for independent tests and some dependence; Benjamini–Yekutieli uses a harmonic-number factor under arbitrary dependence. The page cites Benjamini and Hochberg, JRSS-B, 1995.

title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: a Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
takeaway: Yoav Benjamini and Yosef Hochberg. Procedure: let k be the largest i with ordered p-value P(i) <= (i/m) q*; reject H(1) through H(k). Theorem 1: for independent test statistics and any configuration of false nulls, the procedure controls the FDR at q*. The copy notes received January 1993, revised March 1994.

title: false_discovery_control — SciPy v1.18.0 Manual
takeaway: scipy.stats.false_discovery_control adjusts p-values so that rejecting below a level controls the FDR at that level. method='bh' is Benjamini-Hochberg (default) and method='by' is Benjamini-Yekutieli. Docs cite Benjamini & Hochberg 1995, JRSS-B 57(1):289-300, and Benjamini & Yekutieli 2001, Annals of Statistics.

title: statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests — statsmodels 0.15.0
takeaway: multipletests includes fdr_bh, described as Benjamini/Hochberg (non-negative), and fdr_by, described as Benjamini/Yekutieli (negative). The retrieved page names the methods but does not print the 1995 citation.

title: Optimal Betting Odds against Insider Traders
takeaway: Hyun Song Shin, The Economic Journal, 1991, vol. 101(408), pages 1179-1185. A bookmaker facing some better-informed bettors should post prices by a square-root rule: the ratio of posted prices is the square root of the ratio of winning probabilities. That understates favourites' chances and exaggerates longshots' chances.

title: shin/README.md
takeaway: Python package implementing Shin's method for implied probabilities from bookmaker odds. It estimates an insider proportion z plus probabilities by iteration, and states two-outcome Shin is equivalent to the additive method. References Shin, Economic Journal 1992 (favourite-longshot bias) and 1993 (measuring insider trading), and Štrumbelj, International Journal of Forecasting, 2014.

title: From Biased Odds to Fair Probabilities: Removing the Bookmaker's Overround
takeaway: Martin Eastwood, 14 Sep 2025. penaltyblog.implied.calculate_implied supports multiplicative (divide each raw implied probability by the booksum), power, and Shin (fit z for a mix of informed and uninformed bettors). On 380 Premier League 2024/25 closing-odds matches, multiplicative had the lowest RPS at 0.19724 and Shin was 0.19731; gaps among the top methods were tiny.

title: Implied Odds — penaltyblog documentation
takeaway: Docs say bookmaker overround distorts raw inverse odds, so margin removal is needed before treating prices as probabilities. penaltyblog documents several algorithms for that, including Shin's method.
